brief.headline: Stop paying in advance — move to 30-day credit and free up ₹8.73 L of our cash

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji Industries
priceAsk.target: ₹66.48/KG for Dextrose (a saving of ₹12.95 L per year)
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay them ₹70.80/KG but already buy the same material at ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji Industries — a 6.5% gap. The open-market asking price for this item sits in a ₹60–81/kg band (typically ₹66–73/kg), so our target is fair and we know it's achievable because we're already paying it elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 100% advance payment to standard 30-day credit terms
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹8.73 L of our cash freed up

brief.financialLeverage: They are big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — and growing fast (29.7% per year), so they want new orders. But they keep only 2.9% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, so there's little room for a big price cut without hurting them. We are tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr spend is just 0.07% of their revenue, so on our own we have almost no pull. Their overall health score is D (44/100), meaning they're weak but not in immediate trouble. The play here is to push hard on payment terms (where we have the strongest case) and use the threat of moving volume to Sayaji or another alternate to get them to match our best price — but don't squeeze so hard on price that we destabilise a supplier with thin profit.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹70.80/KG but already get the same Dextrose at ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji Industries
We are paying ₹12.95 L per year more than our cheapest supplier for the same material
We pay them 100% in advance; moving to 30-day credit frees up cash for us
They are growing fast and want new orders
We are a tiny customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹1.06 Cr spend, 0.07% of their ₹1555.82 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They keep very little profit — only 2.9% of every ₹100 they sell

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (current supplier)
alternates.why: Already supplies us Dextrose at ₹66.48/KG — our benchmark price and proof the target is real

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B (62/100) — a drop-in alternate to Sayaji; strong enough to take more volume if we need to move it

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C (57/100) — growing capacity in dextrose, a credible second source to qualify

risks: We are only 0.07% of their revenue, so they can easily walk away — bundle more volume or commit longer to get their attention
Their profit is only 2.9%, so pushing too hard on price could break them or force them to cut quality — focus the squeeze on payment terms and use alternates as leverage for price
We currently pay 100% in advance, so they are used to zero risk from us — they may resist credit terms; be ready to phase it in (e.g. start with 50% advance, then move to 30-day)
They are growing fast (29.7% per year) and may prioritise bigger, faster-growing customers over a small, price-sensitive one like us — lead with volume commitment to stay interesting to them
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to keep buying from you, but right now we're paying you ₹70.80 per kilo and 100% in advance — while we get the same Dextrose at ₹66.48 from Sayaji on better terms, so let's talk about closing that gap and moving you to standard 30-day credit.
